title: PRIMM Semantic Wave Explorer
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Pedagogy
PRIMM
Semantic Waves
Instructional Design
description: Relate each PRIMM stage (Predict, Run, Investigate, Modify, Make) to a point on a semantic wave between concrete and abstract, then place bouncing-ball lesson activities on the stage where each belongs.
audience: Teachers, instructional designers, learning-technology developers and learning-analytics practitioners (college undergraduate and professional development)

educational.topic: PRIMM stages and semantic waves in MicroSim lessons
learningObjectives: The learner will relate each PRIMM stage to a point on a semantic wave and identify which stage a given lesson activity belongs to.
prerequisites: A simple simulation such as the Chapter 1 bouncing ball

accessibility.notes: Stage buttons, the activity select and Reset are native controls; with a card in hand, pressing a stage button places it, so dragging is optional. describe() summarizes the highlighted stage and progress.

controls.label: Activity card
controls.action: drop onto a stage for immediate feedback

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Relate stages to a visual model, then classify activities with feedback
keyQuestions: Why is Predict abstract but Run concrete?
Why does Investigate climb back toward the abstract?
Which stage does a given activity belong to?
commonMisconceptions: That any activity that runs the sim is Run
That Make is the most concrete stage
assessmentOpportunities: Place six activities with no mistakes
Write one activity per stage for a new MicroSim

simulation.modelType: static concept diagram with a placement task
assumptions: Wave heights are illustrative: Predict 0.78, Run 0.18, Investigate 0.72, Modify 0.38, Make 0.60
limitations: A single fixed wave; real lessons vary in shape
